import sys, json, uuid

# The OFFER of this application, and nothing else. Two questions reach this
# cell and no others: the start-up question about what may be called, and a
# call the model actually made. It places no call itself -- it mints the id the
# whole exchange is named by and hands the errand inwards, because the cell
# that talks to a switch is the cell that keeps the book.

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
env = doc.get("envelope") or {}
hdr = env.get("header") or {}
hop = hdr.get("hop") or {}
body = doc.get("body") or {}
route = str(hop.get("route") or "")

SCHEMAS = [
    {"name": "call",
     "description": "Ring somebody up and talk to them. Give the number in "
                    "international form and say in one short line WHY you are "
                    "calling -- the purpose comes back to you the moment the "
                    "person picks up, so you know what to open with. The "
                    "answer to this call arrives when the phone is answered, "
                    "which may be half a minute later; a call nobody takes "
                    "answers `no_answer`, a busy line answers `busy`.",
     "parameters": {"type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "number": {"type": "string",
                                   "description": "the number to ring, in international form, e.g. +4930123456"},
                        "purpose": {"type": "string",
                                    "description": "one short line about why you are calling"}},
                    "required": ["number"]}},
    {"name": "hangup",
     "description": "End a call that is running. With one call on the line you "
                    "need give nothing; with several you MUST say which, by "
                    "the call_id you were told when the call started or when "
                    "it came in -- otherwise the answer lists them and ends "
                    "none. If you are still speaking, the line stays up until "
                    "your sentence is finished -- the answer says so.",
     "parameters": {"type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "call_id": {"type": "string",
                                    "description": "which call to end; only needed when more than one is running"}},
                    "required": []}},
    # THE LINE, and not a call (2.0.0). FreeSWITCH is the proxy: which number
    # reaches this member, and what a caller has to type before it does, live in
    # the SWITCH's own table. These three write that table and read nothing back
    # -- a receipt is the answer, never a listing, because this colony keeps no
    # copy of what it wrote.
    {"name": "add_number",
     "description": "Put a telephone number through to this line. Give it in "
                    "international form. From then on a call from that number "
                    "reaches this conversation -- after the PIN, if one is set. "
                    "This does not ring anybody: it is the door, not a call.",
     "parameters": {"type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "number": {"type": "string",
                                   "description": "the number to let through, in international form, e.g. +4930123456"}},
                    "required": ["number"]}},
    {"name": "set_pin",
     "description": "Ask every caller of this line for a PIN before they are "
                    "put through. Four to eight digits. It replaces whatever "
                    "PIN was set before, and the caller types it on the "
                    "telephone keypad.",
     "parameters": {"type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "pin": {"type": "string",
                                "description": "four to eight digits"}},
                    "required": ["pin"]}},
    {"name": "disable_pin",
     "description": "Stop asking for a PIN. Every number that is on this line "
                    "is put straight through afterwards.",
     "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "required": []}},
]


def out(messages):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(messages))
    sys.exit(0)


def result(tid, text, **header):
    """One tool result. `tid` is the id of the CALL THE MODEL MADE; a header key
    named `call_id` is the id of the telephone call, and the two are different
    things -- which is why this parameter is not called `call_id`."""
    head = {"route": "tool_result", "tool_call_id": tid}
    head.update(header)
    return {"header": head,
            "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                          "id": tid, "text": text}]}


if route == "schemas":
    # The WHOLE offer, whatever list the asker carried: the question is asked
    # of every answerer at once and the collector merges the rows, so an
    # application that filtered by the list would filter itself out of a menu
    # that was never addressed to it.
    out([{"header": {"route": "tool_schemas", "operation": "schemas",
                     "schema_count": len(SCHEMAS), "unknown_count": 0},
          "schemas": SCHEMAS, "unknown": [], "messages": []}])

call_id = str(hop.get("tool_call_id") or "")
name = str(hop.get("tool_name") or "")

# The arguments are the TEXT of the call turn: the name was split off onto
# hop.tool_name one level up.
raw = ""
for m in reversed(body.get("messages") or []):
    if isinstance(m, dict) and isinstance(m.get("text"), str):
        raw = m["text"]
        break
try:
    args = json.loads(raw or "{}")
except ValueError:
    args = None
if not isinstance(args, dict):
    args = None

if name in ("add_number", "set_pin", "disable_pin"):
    # Straight inwards, receipt and all. The cell beside this one is the one
    # that knows the switch, the realm and which member this line belongs to,
    # so it is the one that can say what was written -- this cell would only be
    # guessing, and a receipt that guessed would tell a model a row exists that
    # nobody wrote.
    errand = {"route": "request", "operation": name, "tool_call_id": call_id}
    if name == "add_number":
        errand["number"] = str((args or {}).get("number") or "").strip()
    if name == "set_pin":
        errand["pin"] = str((args or {}).get("pin") or "").strip()
    out([{"header": errand, "messages": []}])

if name == "hangup":
    # WHICH LINE, if the model named one (GH #620). Unreadable arguments are
    # read as none rather than refused: the model asked to end the one call
    # there is, and the half beside this one refuses by itself when there is
    # more than one.
    wanted = str((args or {}).get("call_id") or "").strip()
    out([{"header": {"route": "request", "operation": "hangup",
                     "call_uuid": wanted, "tool_call_id": call_id},
          "messages": []}])

if name != "call":
    out([result(call_id,
                "this application serves `call`, `hangup`, `add_number`, "
                "`set_pin` and `disable_pin`, not `%s`" % name,
                error_code="tool_unknown")])

if args is None:
    out([result(call_id, "the arguments of this call are not a JSON object",
                error_code="invalid_arguments")])

number = str(args.get("number") or "").strip()
if not number:
    out([result(call_id, "`number` is required and was empty",
                error_code="invalid_arguments")])

purpose = str(args.get("purpose") or "").strip()

# The id the WHOLE exchange is named by. It is minted here and nowhere else:
# it becomes FreeSWITCH's `origination_uuid`, the `?session=` of the audio
# fork, and therefore the `session_id` the answer is spoken back into.
call_uuid = str(uuid.uuid4())

# TWO messages out of one call, and they go to two different places: the
# errand itself, inwards, and the RECEIPT the round is waiting for. The receipt
# is immediate on purpose -- the OUTCOME of a telephone call is not a value a
# function returns, it is something that happens, and it arrives as a turn of
# this channel. A tool that waited for it would hold a round open across a
# ringing telephone.
out([
    {"header": {"route": "request", "operation": "call",
                "call_uuid": call_uuid, "number": number,
                "purpose": purpose, "tool_call_id": call_id},
     "messages": []},
    result(call_id,
           "ringing %s. The call runs under call_id %s -- you will be told "
           "when it is answered, and if it is not. Give that id to `hangup` "
           "if more than one call is running." % (number, call_uuid),
           operation="call", session_id=call_uuid, call_id=call_uuid,
           number=number),
])

pin.description: The digits a `set_pin` call carried, on their one hop to the cell that writes them into the switch's own table (2.0.0). Nothing in this colony keeps them; the round they travelled in is logged like every other round.

call_id.description: The call the receipt of a `call` is about, under the name the whole channel now shares (GH #620). Same value as `session_id` on this lane; the second name is what the member's edge promotes to `context.call_id`.

tools.description: the names the asker declares it uses. Read and deliberately ignored: this cell answers with its whole offer, because the question is asked of every answerer at once

description.purpose: The five tools this channel offers an assistant, and the menu entry that makes them callable. Two are about a CALL (`call`, `hangup`) and three are about the LINE (`add_number`, `set_pin`, `disable_pin`): which number reaches this member, and what a caller types before it does. The line lives in the SWITCH's own table, because FreeSWITCH is the proxy -- these three name the errand and the cell beside this one writes it. It mints the id the WHOLE exchange is named by -- FreeSWITCH's `origination_uuid`, the `?session=` of the audio fork, and therefore the session an answer is spoken into -- and hands the errand inwards.
description.use_when: Reached on two questions and no others: the start-up question about what this channel offers, and a tool call the model actually made. Never addressed by name -- the lane and the tool name are what route a call here.
description.not_in_scope: It talks to no switch, keeps no row and knows no call state -- not for a call and not for a line: the three line tools name an errand here and are written one cell over, which is the only cell that knows the switch. Whether a call connected is not its business: that answer arrives as a TURN of this channel, because the outcome of a telephone call is something that happens rather than something a function returns.
description.emits_meaning: route tool_schemas: the whole offer -- `call`, `hangup`, `add_number`, `set_pin` and `disable_pin` -- with `unknown` empty, whatever list the asker carried. route request: the errand, carrying the minted `call_uuid`, the number and the purpose -- or, for a `hangup`, the `call_uuid` the model named, empty where it named none, or, for one of the three line tools, the number or the PIN it carried and nothing else. route tool_result: the receipt of the action under the call's own `tool_call_id` -- for `call` the session the conversation will run under, `hop.error_code` `invalid_arguments` when the arguments could not be read.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: the tool_call turn as it arrived; its `text` is the ARGUMENTS string, because the name was already split off onto hop.tool_name one level up.
examples: a schemas question -> five schemas, `call`, `hangup`, `add_number`, `set_pin` and `disable_pin`, unknown empty
call {number: '+4930…', purpose: 'ask how she slept'} -> a request inwards and a tool_result naming the session
call with no number -> one tool_result, error_code `invalid_arguments`, and no request
hangup {call_id: '…'} -> a request inwards naming that line; hangup with no argument and two calls running -> the half beside this one refuses with `ambiguous_call` and lists them
add_number {number: '+4930…'} -> a request inwards; the receipt comes from the cell that wrote the row, never from here
